questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am half polish so I thought it was a good opportunity to experience the culture and get to learn the language a little better and reconnect with my family.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was so nice and I would give it a 10 if it was easier paper wise, so that we didn't have to fill out so many documents and it was easier to get an overview of the whole process.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy because I arrived one month before the actual exchange started and all the needed information was first send a lot later. I could have used the information before

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a big introduction mail with a long document with all needed information and an online zoom meting where we could ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: But it was due to my early arrival.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy because my mom is polish and found a contact for me so it took one week to get my own apartment. If you don't have a polish contact to help you I wouldn't really recommend finding it completely on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice and quiet. For me it was easy to get everywhere so you don't have to be scared about living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For me it was a long process. The courses I applied for were not all available and I needed to write a lot of emails to finalise my registration process. I even started my semester without my full course schedual and needed to switch some courses after 2 weeks into the semester. Thankfully my mobility coordinates was super sweet and helpfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote a lot of emails to the professors and my mobility coordinator was very helpfull whenever I wrote her an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted but some didn't have space, didn't accept exchange students or was overlapping with some of my other courses. So I would say I got 4/6 I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask more in the beginning of course registration and don't hesitate with sending an email if you are in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses very easy and I didn't get much academic out of them. I was easy to pass without really making any effort and the general lack of effort from the students in my classes made me lose interest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH it is so much more academic and I feel like a can use the knowledge I get from my host university. It is harder to pass but I like the study culture a lot more. I also feel like the teachers are more structured and knows what they are talking about.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. European media regulation: trends and predictions
2. Innovation manager
3. Media and democracy 
4. Me, myselfie and I
5. Management in public relations
6. Managing software projects

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
European media regulation: trends and predictions: The teacher was super nice and generally a course that I accually learned something form.
Me, myselfie and I: Very interesting and the first academic course. Very relevant in this society we live in. 
Managing software projects: interesting and very hands on. Easy to pass.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing (I just spend a lot of money shopping as it is cheaper here in Poland)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, trips around the country, clubbing, dinners, social activities such as ax troughing, candle painting and a lot other things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the introduction week full of activities. There you will meet people that will be your friends for the semester and find a good group to hang out with. Also go to multi pub on Wednesdays and Cubans on Mondays.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a tour starting from old town and down to the central station. Come by BUW and show the rooftop garden and eat at the restaurant OMA.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as I am half Polish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take courses that are not Erasmus courses and preferable courses where you have to make group projects. Then it will be easy to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That everything needs to be done in person and nothing is done online.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The sweetness and openness when you go and visit polish families.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember to drink water when you are trying the local alcohols. 
2. Be open, the place you are visiting is very nice and not as bad as the internet pre trays it to be. 
3. Go enjoy the cheep city life. Go to a lot of cafes and live your life as you where the queen/king because now you have the money to do so.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy the 3 moths public transport card when you arrive. It is so much cheaper than buying tickets every time you take the public transport.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many awesome people form all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get the paperwork in order and register for my classes

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
